requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale: The tests adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`. I read the whole test module in `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs`, along with the `pages` and `entry` code those tests call. I used the code only to see what the tests render, not to judge correctness. Obligations and the tests that cover them: - **Show each `habeas:coverage` citation on the file root or an explicit function or method.** - `notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs` has a root citation, a free function, an impl method, and an inline citation on `fn[unexplained]`. It checks that each appears as an entry: `File root`, `fn[ordinary]`, `impl[Worker]/fn[work]` and `fn[unexplained]`. - It also checks that a citation on `mod nested` is not shown (`Nested module must` is absent) and that the nested function's doc comment does not leak (`Child documentation` is absent). - `citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations` checks that a module citation and citation text inside a string literal produce no entry. It asserts the "No coverage explanations are present" message and the absence of `exception proposal` and `Module only.`. - **Identify the source item and its source location.** The first test checks, for each of the four entries, the `Source: code.rs:{first}–{last}` line range and the `First source citation at line N` line. It also checks the heading label (`File root` or the item selector). - **Show fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments.** - The first test covers root `//!` docs, `///` docs, a `/** */` method doc, and fenced commentary on the root, a function and a method. - It also checks that commentary is HTML-escaped (`<unsafe>`, with no raw ``). - `justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments` covers three cases: - docs alone give a `### Rust doc comments` section; - fenced commentary alone gives a `### Citation commentary` section; - an ordinary non-doc comment alone supplies no justification and is not shown. - **Say so when no tracked justification is present.** - `fn[unexplained]` has an inline citation and no docs. Its entry must contain `No tracked justification is present.` and no `Rust doc comments` heading. - The test also counts that message exactly once, so justified entries do not carry it. - The ordinary-comment case in the second test asserts the message too. - **Label file-root citations as file-threshold exception proposals and function or method citations as function exception proposals.** The first test counts `File-threshold exception proposal` exactly once and `Function exception proposal` exactly three times (`ordinary`, `work`, `unexplained`). The absent-labels check in the module-citation test covers the negative case. A possible further case is several `habeas:coverage` citations on one item, which the implementation merges. The requirement's entry model is per source item and does not clearly separate that case. I don't treat it as a named boundary, so I don't count it as a gap. The tests carry {test} references to the subject. Assertions are on rendered content, not just execution. I found no uncovered obligation and no acknowledgment is needed.

:::{req} index.file_map.notes
Each listed first-party Rust file in the combined file coverage
map MUST provide access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
